With a speech to text API, you can add audio transcription features to the apps and systems you’re already using. These APIs have use cases across a wide range of industries. They’re helpful for transcribing customer service calls, subtitling videos, taking meeting notes, or even creating clinical documentation.

With so many speech to text APIs available to choose from, the best option for your organization will depend on your goals. Some teams prioritize high accuracy rates or low latency, while others value multilingual support. Here’s what to consider when choosing a speech to text API for your project.

## Summary

• The right speech to text API depends on your organization’s needs and goals.

• Accuracy, latency, pricing, and multilingual coverage are all top considerations when choosing an API.

• High accuracy rates are most important for regulated industries, but may not be necessary for more casual use cases.

• Customer service and call center teams should also consider factors like diarization, timestamp accuracy, entity detection, and conversation intelligence.

• Speech to text APIs perform best with clean audio that has background noise removed.

## Measure speech to text API accuracy beyond benchmark scores

Speech to text accuracy rates can vary depending on the quality of the underlying audio, so the API may not consistently reach its benchmark scores. Instead of relying entirely on benchmarks to make your decision, test the API using real-world speech that’s appropriate for your planned use case.

As you test the API, monitor the word error rate to determine if the output is accurate enough for your needs. You’ll also want to weigh accuracy against cost to decide which API is right for you.

If you’re in a highly regulated industry like healthcare, law, or finance, you might prefer to pay more for an API that can deliver consistently high accuracy rates, regardless of audio quality. However, if your budget is limited, you might choose to sacrifice some accuracy for affordability.

## Assess real-time speech to text API latency and reliability

Another factor to consider when choosing your speech to text API is latency, or the length of the delay between the audio and the transcription. When evaluating API options, run a latency test with real-world call conditions, instead of just transcribing sample audio.

This is a particularly important consideration if you’re using the API to transcribe meetings or customer calls in real time. If the latency is too high, the model will transcribe speech much slower than it actually happens, resulting in a poor user experience.

On top of that, you’ll also need to consider the API’s overall reliability. Professional speech to text tools often need to transcribe multiple audio files at the same time. The most reliable APIs can handle several projects concurrently without sacrificing accuracy or latency.

## Compare speech to text API pricing, scale, and total cost

While reliable performance is essential for an audio transcription API , you’ll also need to consider your budget. If your budget is limited, you’ll need to find an API that balances consistency and affordability.

Speech to text APIs are often priced per-character, per-word, or per-minute of audio transcribed. Some APIs also charge a flat monthly subscription rate, while others allow you to pay as you go.

Your API provider might offer volume discounts, which can help keep costs in check if you’re transcribing at scale. However, most plans also have monthly subscription limits, and you could end up paying overage fees if you exceed them. When choosing an API, consider how discounts and limits could affect your total monthly spend.

When evaluating pricing, think about how many files you need to transcribe each month and if you plan on scaling up in the future. If you’re transcribing a large volume of audio, you may need to sacrifice some accuracy to keep costs in check.

Infrastructure costs are another important consideration if you’re transcribing audio at scale. Many businesses consider self-hosting with an open-source transcription model to cut back on costs. However, if you go this route, you’ll need to pay for and maintain your own digital infrastructure, which could end up costing more than an API. With a managed speech to text API, you’re not paying hosting and storage costs for your speech to text projects.

## Review multilingual coverage options

If your business has an international presence or multilingual customer base, you’ll need a speech to text API that supports all the languages you do business in. When comparing your API options, review the number of languages currently available, then do a test for each of the languages you want to transcribe.

Then, evaluate the API’s performance for each test. The transcription model should deliver similar accuracy and latency across each language.

Even if your business currently operates in just one language, you may need multilingual support in the future. When choosing a multilingual speech recognition API, consider your long-term plans and whether you might expand to other countries as you grow.

## Check security and data controls for industry compliance

Before committing to an API, make sure it meets your industry’s compliance standards and data privacy standards for the country and state you’re operating in. If your speech to text API isn’t compliant, it could introduce security and privacy risks for both your business and your customers.
